label: Current Detention Population
source: Austin Kocher / Deportation Data Project (data as of Jul 11, 2026; released Jul 24)
deltaNote: ICE went dark on its congressionally-mandated biweekly detention/deportation reports after its Apr 9, 2026 release (60,311 held); the Jul 24, 2026 release was the first new data in over 3 months, showing 65,765 held as of Jul 11 — up from 60,311 in April but below the Jan 24, 2026 record of 70,766. 70.6% (46,436 of 65,765) have no criminal conviction. GPS/ankle-monitor caseload continued climbing past 35,000. Republicans omitted the biweekly-reporting mandate from FY2026 appropriations language for the first time since 2018; ICE blamed the gap on government shutdowns.

label: Detainees w/ No Criminal Conviction
contestNote: ICE counts misdemeanors and traffic violations as 'criminal'; advocates dispute the framing. 42,722 of 60,311 detainees have no conviction.

label: Deaths in ICE Custody (FY2025)
contestNote: DWN counts 31 for calendar year 2025 — all-time high; ICE uses fiscal year; both are records

label: 287(g) MOAs Active
contestNote: ACLU's 'Deputized for Disaster' analysis found 77.2M people (32% of the country) now live in a county with a 287(g) agreement, with DHS training 10,000+ officers under the model and expansion reaching university police, state fire marshals, and wildlife agencies in some states. Virginia's HB1441/SB783 (effective July 1, 2026) restricts state 287(g) participation, while local sheriffs continue independently. New Mexico, Maine, and Maryland enacted bans. 2,127 MOAs as of mid-July 2026 across 39 states and 2 territories — up from 1,903 on June 5 and 688 when Trump's second term began in January 2025. As of Aug 6, 2026, ICE reports 2,179 total MOAs across 39 states and 2 territories — 179 JEM agreements (30 states + 1 territory), 533 WSO agreements (34 states), and 1,467 TFM agreements (32 states + 2 territories) — up from 2,127 in mid-July.

label: Alternatives to Detention (ATD)
source: Austin Kocher / Deportation Data Project (data as of Jul 11, 2026)
deltaNote: GPS ankle-monitor/ATD caseload continued climbing as of the Jul 24, 2026 data release (first since April), up from 179,991 total ATD enrollment reported in Feb 2026 filings; the 35,000+ figure reflects the actively-monitored GPS cohort specifically.

label: Deaths in Custody (FY2026, partial)
source: NBC News / AP / ICE.gov (as of Aug 4, 2026)
contestNote: At least 24 people have died in ICE custody in calendar year 2026 through Aug 4 — surpassing the pace of every prior year on record except FY2025. New deaths since the June 25 HRW/PHR report include Jesús Manuel Arenas-Silva (45, Venezuela), who died of suspected cardiac arrest July 13 while being bus-transferred from Irwin County Detention Center to Folkston, GA — his family says ICE denied him his medications — and Priciliano Trejo (29, Mexico), who died July 24 at Stewart Detention Center after his family says a leukemia diagnosis went untreated. Acting Director Venturella's June 4 memo ending post-release death reporting remains in effect, and DHS has not restored the OIDO oversight office shuttered May 5.
deltaNote: Up from 21+ reported through Jul 6, 2026; two additional named deaths (Arenas-Silva Jul 13, Trejo Jul 24) documented since the June 25 HRW/PHR report.

label: FY2025 Total Removals (Trump Year 1)
contestNote: ICE combines ~330,000 formal removals and ~110,000 voluntary returns — a methodology that inflates comparisons to prior administrations. Formal removals alone do not exceed FY2013 record of 432,201. ICE has now set an official target of 1 million removals per year. Total since inauguration (Jan 2025 through ~May 7, 2026): ~570,000, per Border Czar Tom Homan (NPR, May 7, 2026). FY2026 pace: ~1,286 removals/day as of April 4 — annualized ~470,000.
deltaNote: vs. ~271,000 in FY2024; total since inauguration: ~570,000 (Homan, May 7, 2026)

label: Weekly ICE Arrests (Post-Minneapolis Avg)
source: AP / UC Berkeley Deportation Data Project (Apr 25, 2026)
deltaNote: Down from 8,347/week (5-wk avg) before Feb 4, 2026 after Minneapolis agent pullback. Dec 2025 peak was ~40,000/month. Non-criminal share fell from 46% to 41%. Arrests surged in KY, IN, NC, and FL despite national decline.

label: Detainees Held Over 1 Year
deltaNote: Up from 998 in October 2025, more than doubling in 6 months as ICE detention expansion accelerates. The El Gamal family — Egyptian mother and 5 children — spent 320+ days in detention before their release April 26, 2026 following an aborted deportation flight.

label: ICE/CBP 'Secure America Act' — Signed Into Law
source: White House / CBS News / CNBC / Al Jazeera (June 10, 2026)
contestNote: Senate passed 52-47 on June 5; House passed 214-212 on a near-party-line vote June 9; Trump signed the 'Secure America Act' into law at an Oval Office ceremony June 10, 2026. Final breakdown: ~$38.5B ICE enforcement/detention (incl. $7B for HSI agents), $26B CBP, ~$5B DHS discretionary enforcement, $3.5B border technology. The $1.776B anti-weaponization settlement fund for Trump political allies survived all Democratic amendments. No independent oversight provisions, no minimum medical care standards, no use-of-force accountability despite record FY2026 custody deaths. Combined with $45B+ already in H.R. 1 (Big Beautiful Bill, signed July 4, 2025), total new immigration enforcement funding now exceeds $115B — the largest single immigration enforcement appropriation in U.S. history, locked in through the end of Trump's term. Rand Paul (R-KY) and Sen. Lisa Murkowski (R-AK) were the only Republican holdouts.
deltaNote: House passed 214-212 (June 9); Trump signed June 10. Total 2025-2026 immigration enforcement allocation now exceeds $115B — roughly 13× ICE's FY2024 base budget of $9.1B annually.

label: Asylum Grant Rate (Trump 2nd Term)
contestNote: White House claims rate fell from 50%+ under Biden to 7% under Trump, attributing it to restored 'rule of law.' Advocates say decline reflects reduced court capacity, policy barriers, and denial of access to counsel rather than merit determinations.
deltaNote: Down from 50%+ grant rate under Biden administration

label: ICE Congressionally-Mandated Data Reporting Gap
source: The Marshall Project / KJZZ / Austin Kocher (Jul 2026)
contestNote: ICE went without publishing its biweekly detention/arrest/deportation data — mandated by appropriations law every year since 2018 — from its Apr 9, 2026 report until a partial release Jul 24, 2026. FY2026 appropriations language notably omitted the reporting mandate for the first time. ICE blamed government shutdowns; researchers and advocates (Center for Immigration Studies' Jessica Vaughan, American Immigration Council's Aaron Reichlin-Melnick, NILC's Heidi Altman) say the agency has ample funding ($240B+) and other agencies kept publishing on schedule. DHS separately claims 981,000 arrests and 948,000 deportations since Jan 2025, plus 3M+ total departures including 2.2M self-deportations — figures that cannot be independently verified absent the underlying data.
